citations.quote: A genuine single family office arrangement, established to serve the investment needs of members of a single family, which is not being run as a business (i.e. not receiving any income, other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family) or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective, should not in the ordinary course be considered as carrying on a business from a licensing perspective.

readings.distinction: The rival parses place “or” inside or outside the scope of “not”. Here it is inside: not (business or profit objective), equivalent to both absences. This reading is contextually preferable because the surrounding paragraph identifies profit-making purpose as a business indicator, although the awkward coordination prevents certainty. [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] means only that the disputed antecedent holds.

citations.quote: A genuine single family office arrangement, established to serve the investment needs of members of a single family, which is not being run as a business (i.e. not receiving any income, other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family) or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective, should not in the ordinary course be considered as carrying on a business from a licensing perspective.

readings.distinction: Here “or” is outside the first predicate's negation: (not business) or profit objective. Consequently, the second alternative requires the presence of a profit objective, not its absence. This repairs the prior mismatch between the stated narrow-negation parse and its formula. The reading is syntactically arguable but contextually weaker because it allows a profit objective to satisfy the antecedent. [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] means only that this disputed antecedent holds.

vocabulary_concerns: The supplied income_beyond_reimbursement fact operationalizes the parenthetical but cannot independently represent the broader case-specific assessment of being run as a business, including continuity, occupation or duty, and capability of making profit.
The irregular coordination “which is not … or have” leaves negation attachment uncertain. Separate predicates express the rival outcomes but do not resolve the wording.

The previous disjunction of two absences would require an additional assumption supplying a separate negative to the second alternative. It does not follow from the stated business-only negation and is not retained as that parse.
The Boolean result expresses only antecedent satisfaction. It does not encode “should not in the ordinary course”, regulatory intent, or a complete licensing conclusion.
